chat.disclaimer.text.value: RecoFree is geen vervanging voor professionele hulp.

chat.modal.body.value:
{companionName} is an AI companion, not a therapist or doctor.

• RecoFree does not replace professional mental health care.
• RecoFree never provides diagnoses or medical advice.
• RecoFree is not a replacement for a psychologist or psychiatrist.
• Sometimes professional help is the better choice — and that is okay.
• In case of crisis, always contact a professional or call 1813.
• Your conversations are private and stay on your device.

diary.quote.1.text.value: "You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength."

diary.quote.2.text.value: "We suffer more often in imagination than in reality."

diary.quote.3.text.value: "The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts."

diary.quote.4.text.value: "It is not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters."

diary.quote.5.text.value: "No man is free who is not master of himself."

diary.quote.6.text.value: "Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life."

diary.quote.7.text.value: "The best revenge is not to be like your enemy."

diary.quote.8.text.value: "Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one."

diary.quote.9.text.value: "He who fears death will never do anything worthy of a living man."

diary.quote.10.text.value: "First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do."

diary.quote.11.text.value: "The soul becomes dyed with the colour of its thoughts."

diary.quote.12.text.value: "Difficulties strengthen the mind, as labor does the body."

diary.quote.13.text.value: "Man is not worried by real problems so much as by his imagined anxieties about real problems."

diary.quote.14.text.value: "Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking."

diary.quote.15.text.value: "If it is not right, do not do it. If it is not true, do not say it."

diary.journal_explanation.value: Writing like the Stoics — what could you control today, what not? What happened, and how did you respond?

diary.gratitude_explanation.value: Your brain automatically looks for danger and problems. Writing three things that were good trains your mind to notice what is good too. Not because everything is fine — but because both exist.
